note: Rewritten from the species-level description by Bourguignon & Roisin (2011), the original in English; the soldier and the alate are described. The measurements keep the mm unit of the original; abbreviations are given in parentheses at their first occurrence, after which only the measurement names are used.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier has a large, rounded head, a large fontanelle aperture clearly visible from above, mandibles strongly curved at the apex and an elongate pronotum; these characters separate it from the other species of New Guinea.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head rounded, densely hairy; compound eyes large; pronotum wide and elongate, with many medium-sized and large setae; antennae 20—22-segmented. Measurements (mm, 8 individuals of the type colony; in parentheses 4 individuals of another colony): total body length (TBL) 8.27—8.99 (7.81—8.12); head length to clypeus (HLC) 1.53—1.87 (1.48—1.62); head width including eyes (HWE) 1.84—1.96 (1.79—1.81); pronotum length (PL) 1.04—1.12 (1.02—1.07); pronotum width (PW) 1.63—1.70 (1.59—1.61); forewing length (FWL) n.a. (13—13.2); eye diameter (ED) 0.45—0.50 (0.45—0.5).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body large. Head rounded, with about 40 setae; fontanelle aperture large, its opening clearly visible from above; antennae usually 16-segmented; pronotum elongate, with about 70 setae, mostly along the margins; mesonotum, metanotum and abdomen with many setae; mandibles strongly curved at the apex. Measurements (mm, 99 individuals from 33 colonies): head length to fontanelle (HLF) 1.11—1.47; head length including mandibles (HLL) 1.70—2.20; head width (HW) 1.21—1.54; pronotum length (PL) 0.38—0.64; pronotum width (PW) 0.77—1.03; right mandible length (RML) 0.97—1.20; postmentum width (MPW) 0.30—0.49; hind tibia length (T3L) 1.05—1.34.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Widely distributed in the forests of New Guinea, also known from New Ireland; the literature also records it from the Malay Peninsula to the Sunda region.
